source.title: Large Neural Networks Learning from Scratch with Very Few Data and without Explicit Regularization

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; PDF text extraction has some line-break and layout artifacts, but the relevant training and result descriptions are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests zero training error and generalization on real image labels in fine-grained image classification using several CNN architectures, datasets and small training subsets. It does not test random labels or the other specified interventions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that cited prior work memorizes random labels and random image data, but that is not its own result. Its experiments use the real dataset labels; no random-label, shuffled-pixel, Gaussian-noise, corrupted-label, training-time comparison, or real-versus-random learning-order result is reported.
record.test_reason: The study tests the real-label generalization part of V5 in a new setting: CNNs trained from scratch on small image datasets without weight decay, dropout or augmentation. Random-label memorization is cited prior work, not an experimental result.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate, but strong test accuracy is setting-dependent. The authors conclude that very large CNNs can generalize from few real-label examples without augmentation, explicit regularization or pretraining, despite zero training error. They also emphasize dataset-dependent architecture rankings and restrict their empirical findings to CNN image classification.
record.recipe_differences: Uses real-label fine-grained image classification with small training subsets rather than random-label memorization; uses ResNet018, ResNet101 and VGG19 with Lamb and a fixed 300-epoch schedule.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and architecture change test accuracy and which model ranks best; the paper says model ranking was consistent over the training-set sizes studied.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning and Computing
record.problems: The experiments cover CNNs and image classification only, and use five seeds per configuration. The paper does not test random labels or report random-label training behavior; the random-label statement in its introduction refers to cited work. Caltech2 values across training-set sizes are mainly presented in a figure.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted. Rows record the reported real-label test accuracies and explicitly stated training-error result; the figure-only Caltech2 points are not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, their training error and chance-level test performance, with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
True-versus-random-label training time and convergence across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training fit and test-error trajectories across random-label corruption fractions.

Whether explicit regularization prevents fitting random labels; separate effects of weight decay, dropout and augmentation; matched regularized controls measuring the performance change caused by removal.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy or random labels.

missing.what: Table 3's full-training-set real-label results without explicit regularization are omitted despite rows_left_out claiming no omissions: CUB accuracies 22.66/29.96/24.99%; aircraft 49.88/58.91/68.78%; flowers 54.66/54.87/53.05%; cars 20.33/24.34/16.14%, respectively for ResNet018/ResNet101/VGG19. These also bear on V5's real-label clause.
missing.locator: Section 3, Table 3; training conditions and zero training error in Section 2.3.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly treats all of V5 as untested. Its real-label clause is separable from random-label fitting. Low absolute accuracies alone do not show that removing regularization caused poor generalization, so those rows warrant no challenge verdict. No result tests V1–V4 or V6.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment uses completely random labels or reports test error at chance under random labels.
No comparison of training time for true versus random labels or convergence speed across corruption fractions.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiment.
No experiment varies the fraction of randomly corrupted labels.
No explicit regularization comparison under random labels; the study trains without augmentation, weight decay, or dropout on real labels only.
No experiment compares when real-label patterns and noisy or random labels are learned.
